<!-- definition-1: body_md -->
In a finite abelian group $G$, a set $A\subseteq G$ has the \emph{$k$-order property} if there are elements $a_1,\dots,a_k$ and $b_1,\dots,b_k$ in $G$ such that
\[
 a_p+b_q\in A \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad p\le q.
\]
Equivalently, the relation $a+b\in A$ contains a half-graph of height $k$. The set $A$ is \emph{$k$-stable} if it has no $k$-order property.
<!-- end definition-1 -->
<!-- lemma-1: body_md -->
\label{lem:dimensions}
For every $i\ge1$, we have $d_i\ge\operatorname{twr}(i-1)$. If $d=d_s$, then
\[
 n=d+\log_2d+3,
 \qquad
 d\ge\frac12\log_2|G|.
\]
<!-- end lemma-1 -->
<!-- proof-1: body_md -->
The tower bound is immediate for $i\le4$ and then follows from
\[
 d_{i+1}=2^{D_i-3}\ge2^{d_i}.
\]
Also $d=2^{D_{s-1}-3}$, so $D_{s-1}=\log_2d+3$ and hence $n=d+\log_2d+3$. Since $\log_2d+3\le d$ for $d\ge8$, we have $d\ge n/2$.
<!-- end proof-1 -->
<!-- proposition-1: body_md -->
\label{prop:HLMregularity}
The only $\varepsilon$-regular subspace for $f$ is $\{0\}$. Its index is
\[
 |G|=2^n\ge\operatorname{twr}(s).
\]
<!-- end proposition-1 -->
<!-- proof-2: body_md -->
The zero subspace $H=\{0\}$ is vacuously $\varepsilon$-regular because $H^\perp=G$.

Let $H\subseteq G$ be a nonzero subspace. Choose the least $i$ for which some $v\in H$ has $v^i\ne0$. Every element of $H$ then vanishes on the earlier blocks. For $g\in G$, let $\gamma_g\in G$ be supported on block $i$, with
\[
 \gamma_g^i=\xi_i(g^{<i}),
\]
and call $g$ good if $\gamma_g\notin H^\perp$. If $i\le3$, then a nonzero functional on $\mathbb F_2^{d_i}$ is nonzero on some basis vector, so at least a $1/d_i\ge1/8$ fraction of prefixes are good. If $i>3$, then \eqref{eq:spanning} shows that more than a quarter of the prefixes are good.

Fix a good $g\in G$ and average over vectors $w\in G$ supported on blocks $i+1,\dots,s$. Put
\[
 X_w:=\widehat{f|_{g+w+H}}(\gamma_g).
\]
Then
\[
 \mathbb E_wX_w=\frac1{2s}.
\]
Indeed, the terms $B_j$ with $j<i$ have zero coefficient at $\gamma_g$, the term $B_i$ contributes $1/2$, and for $j>i$ averaging first over the fresh $j$th block replaces $B_j$ with the constant $1/2$, which has zero coefficient at $\gamma_g\notin H^\perp$.

Since $\gamma_g\notin H^\perp$ and $0\le f\le1$, we have $|X_w|\le1/2$. If $q$ is the fraction of $w$ with $X_w>\varepsilon$, then
\[
 \frac1{2s}\le\frac q2+(1-q)\varepsilon,
\]
and $\varepsilon\le1/(16s)$ gives $q\ge7/(8s)$.
Adding such a vector $w$ does not change $\gamma_g$, and for uniform $g\in G$ the sum $g+w$ is uniform in $G$. Hence more than
\[
 \frac18\cdot\frac7{8s}=\frac7{64s}>\varepsilon
\]
of the points of $G$ lie in $H$-cosets that are not $\varepsilon$-uniform. Since every $H$-coset has the same size, more than an $\varepsilon$-fraction of the cosets are not $\varepsilon$-uniform. Thus no nonzero $H$ is $\varepsilon$-regular. Finally, Lemma~\ref{lem:dimensions} gives $2^n\ge\operatorname{twr}(s)$.
<!-- end proof-2 -->
<!-- theorem-1: body_md -->
The HLM set $A_s$, with $d=d_s$, has the $d$-order property. Hence
\[
 h(A_s)\ge d\ge\operatorname{twr}(s-1).
\]
<!-- end theorem-1 -->
<!-- proof-3: body_md -->
By \eqref{eq:spanning}, we may choose a basis $v_1,\dots,v_d$ of $U$ from $\Xi_s$ and prefixes $w_1,\dots,w_d\in W$ with $\xi_s(w_\ell)=v_\ell$. Let $v_1^*,\dots,v_d^*\in U$ be the dual basis, and for $1\le m\le d$ set
\[
 z_m:=\sum_{j=m+1}^d v_j^*.
\]
Then $\langle z_m,v_\ell\rangle=[\ell>m]$. Taking
\[
 a_\ell:=(w_\ell,0),
 \qquad
 b_m:=(0,z_m)
\]
gives $a_\ell+b_m\in A_s$ exactly when $\ell\le m$.
<!-- end proof-3 -->
<!-- lemma-2: body_md -->
\label{lem:sauer}
Let $N:=|W|$ and $r\ge1$. If $C\subseteq W\times U$ is $r$-stable, then
\[
 \bigl|\{R_C(u):u\in U\}\bigr|
 \le\sum_{j=0}^{r-1}\binom Nj.
\]
Moreover, for $1\le q\le N/2$,
\[
 \sum_{j=0}^q\binom Nj\le\left(\frac{\mathrm eN}{q}\right)^q.
\]
<!-- end lemma-2 -->
<!-- proof-4: body_md -->
If $w_1,\dots,w_r\in W$ are shattered by the row traces, then choosing $u_1,\dots,u_r$ in $U$ so that $w_\ell\in R_C(u_m)$ exactly when $\ell\le m$ gives $(w_\ell,0)+(0,u_m)\in C$ exactly when $\ell\le m$. Since $C$ is $r$-stable, no $r$ elements of $W$ are shattered, so the row family has VC dimension at most $r-1$. Sauer's lemma \cite{Sauer} then gives the first bound, and the second is the standard binomial-sum estimate.
<!-- end proof-4 -->
<!-- theorem-2: body_md -->
\label{thm:top-robust}
For the HLM set $A_s$ with $d=d_s$, we have
\[
 h_{1/16}(A_s)\ge\frac d8\ge\operatorname{twr}(s-2).
\]
<!-- end theorem-2 -->
<!-- proof-5: body_md -->
Set $A=A_s$, $N=|W|=8d$, and $r=d/8$. For distinct $u,v\in U$, the traces $R_A(u)$ and $R_A(v)$ differ exactly at those $w\in W$ for which
\[
 \langle u+v,\xi_s(w)\rangle=1.
\]
By \eqref{eq:spanning}, this equality holds for more than $N/4$ values of $w$. Thus the $2^d$ row traces form a binary code of length $N$ and minimum distance greater than $N/4$.

Let $C\subseteq G$ be $r$-stable and let $M$ be its number of distinct row traces. Lemma~\ref{lem:sauer} gives
\[
 M\le\sum_{j=0}^{r-1}\binom Nj
 \le(64\mathrm e)^r
 =2^d\left(\frac{\mathrm e}{4}\right)^r.
\]
Because the original traces are more than $N/4$ apart, a trace of $C$ can be within $N/8$ of at most one of them. Hence
\[
 \frac{|A\triangle C|}{|G|}
 >\frac18\left(1-\frac{M}{2^d}\right)
 \ge\frac18\left(1-\left(\frac{\mathrm e}{4}\right)^r\right)
 >\frac1{16},
\]
since $r\ge3$ and $\mathrm e<3$.
Therefore no set differing from $A$ on at most $|G|/16$ points is $r$-stable, so $h_{1/16}(A)\ge r$. For $t=\operatorname{twr}(s-2)$, we have $t\ge16$, and Lemma~\ref{lem:dimensions} gives $d\ge2^t$. Since $2^t\ge8t$ for $t\ge16$, we obtain $d/8\ge t$.
<!-- end proof-5 -->
<!-- lemma-3: body_md -->
\label{lem:fibre}
For every choice of $\xi_1,\dots,\xi_{s-1}$, there exist a value $c_0$, a set $F_0\subseteq c^{-1}(c_0)$ of size $m$, and an injective map $\xi_s:W\to U\setminus\{0\}$ satisfying the spanning condition \eqref{eq:spanning} such that
\[
 16\mid m,
 \qquad
 \frac{2d}{\sqrt s}\le m\le\frac{3d}4,
\]
and the vectors $\{\xi_s(w):w\in F_0\}$ are linearly independent.
<!-- end lemma-3 -->
<!-- proof-6: body_md -->
Let $F=c^{-1}(c_0)$ be a largest fibre. The central-binomial bound gives
\[
 |F|=8d\,2^{-(s-1)}\binom{s-1}{\lfloor(s-1)/2\rfloor}
 \ge\frac{4d}{\sqrt s}.
\]
Since $s\ge16$, we have $3d/\sqrt s\le\min\{|F|,3d/4\}$, and Lemma~\ref{lem:dimensions} gives $d/\sqrt s>16$. Thus the interval $[2d/\sqrt s,3d/\sqrt s]$ contains a multiple $m$ of $16$, and we may choose $F_0\subseteq F$ of size $m$.

Choose the $8d$ values $\xi_s(w)$ independently and uniformly from $U$. The probability of a zero value, a collision, a hyperplane containing at least $6d$ values, or a dependence among the values on $F_0$ is at most
\[
 8d\,2^{-d}
 +\binom{8d}{2}2^{-d}
 +\left(\frac2{\mathrm e}\right)^d
 +2^{m-d}<1.
\]
Here the final inequality uses $m\le3d/4$ and $d\ge256$. The third term follows from Hoeffding's inequality and a union bound over hyperplanes; the fourth follows by exposing the $m$ vectors successively. Some choice therefore avoids all four events. It is injective and nonzero, satisfies \eqref{eq:spanning}, and is independent on $F_0$.
<!-- end proof-6 -->
<!-- theorem-3: body_md -->
\label{thm:threshold}
For every choice of $\xi_1,\dots,\xi_{s-1}$, there exist an injective map $\xi_s:W\to U\setminus\{0\}$ satisfying the spanning condition \eqref{eq:spanning} and a threshold $\theta$ such that for
\[
 S:=\{x\in G:f(x)\ge\theta\}
\]
we have
\[
 h_\varepsilon(S)\ge\frac d{8\sqrt s}\ge\operatorname{twr}(s-2).
\]
<!-- end theorem-3 -->
<!-- proof-7: body_md -->
Take $c_0$, $F_0$, $m$, and $\xi_s$ from Lemma~\ref{lem:fibre} and set $\theta=(c_0+1)/s$. Since $\sum_{j<s}B_j(w,u)=c(w)=c_0$ for $(w,u)\in F_0\times U$, we have
\[
 (w,u)\in S
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 \langle u,\xi_s(w)\rangle=0.
\]
Since the $m$ vectors $\xi_s(w)$ for $w\in F_0$ are independent, the traces on $F_0$ run through all $2^m$ binary patterns, each $2^{d-m}$ times.

Let $E\subseteq G$ satisfy $|E|\le\varepsilon|G|$. The edit density on $F_0\times U$ is at most
\[
 \delta:=\frac{8\varepsilon d}{m}
 \le4\varepsilon\sqrt s
 \le\frac1{4\sqrt s}
 \le\frac1{16}.
\]
At least half the elements $u\in U$ have at most $2\delta m\le m/8$ edits on $F_0\times\{u\}$. Since each original trace has $2^{d-m}$ representatives, at least $2^{m-1}$ original traces have such a representative. A Hamming ball of radius $m/8$ has size at most
\[
 V:=\sum_{j=0}^{m/8}\binom mj\le(8\mathrm e)^{m/8},
\]
so $S\triangle E$ has at least $2^{m-1}/V$ distinct traces on $F_0$.

Since
\[
 V(16\mathrm e)^{m/16}
 \le(8\mathrm e)^{m/8}(16\mathrm e)^{m/16}
 =2^m\left(\frac{\mathrm e^3}{64}\right)^{m/16}
 <2^{m-1},
\]
this number of traces exceeds $(16\mathrm e)^{m/16}$. Applying Lemma~\ref{lem:sauer} on $F_0\times U$ shows that $S\triangle E$ is not $(m/16)$-stable, so
\[
 h_\varepsilon(S)\ge\frac m{16}\ge\frac d{8\sqrt s}.
\]

For $t=\operatorname{twr}(s-2)$, Lemma~\ref{lem:dimensions} gives $d\ge2^t$ and $s\le t$. Since $2^t\ge8t^{3/2}$ for $t\ge16$, we obtain $d/(8\sqrt s)\ge t$.
<!-- end proof-7 -->
